citations.title: Assisted Living Programs (definition, levels, penalties)
citations.requirement: Statutory basis for licensing assisted living programs. COMAR 10.07.14 implements it.

citations.title: Assisted living manager training
citations.requirement: Manager completes an 80-hour OHCQ-approved course with an exam. Manager then completes 20 hours of continuing education every 2 years. Penalty of up to $10,000.

citations.title: Assisted living manager licensure (Board of Long-Term Care Administrators)
citations.requirement: Assisted living manager licensure is required from July 1, 2026. The interim provisional period is up to 90 days, extendable up to 30 days (§9-3A-01(b)(2) per SB 613 enacted text).

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Defines certified medication technician, delegation of nursing tasks, Resident Assessment Tool, incident, significant change and protective device. Use these exact terms in the manual.

citations.title: License Required
citations.requirement: License is issued for a number of beds and a level of care. The license is displayed in a common-use area (§G).

citations.title: Levels of Care
citations.requirement: Level 1 (low), Level 2 (moderate) and Level 3 (high). A resident may be served only within the licensed level.

citations.title: Licensing Procedure
citations.requirement: Application, business plan and 1-year budget, and plan of correction. OHCQ may issue a provisional license. No operation before a license or provisional license is issued. An incomplete application may be closed after 180 days.

citations.title: Changes in an Assisted Living Program that Affect the Operating License
citations.requirement: Notify OHCQ immediately of application changes. Report code citations within 7 days. Get OHCQ approval before adding beds or raising the level. Give 60 days' notice (49 or fewer beds) of ownership change, relocation or closure. SDAT good standing is required (§H).

citations.title: Licensure Standards Waiver
citations.requirement: Written waiver request citing the regulation and hardship. OHCQ decides within 45 days of a complete request.

citations.title: Uniform Disclosure Statement
citations.requirement: Complete the Uniform Disclosure Statement on the OHCQ form. Give it free to anyone who asks and include it in marketing materials. File an amended statement within 30 days of a service change.

citations.title: Compliance Monitoring
citations.requirement: OHCQ conducts an annual on-site survey. The interval may extend to 18 months if there is no open plan of correction, complaint, civil money penalty or sanction.

citations.title: Administration
citations.requirement: Written quality assurance plan. Manager and delegating nurse meet every 6 months (§A(2)(b)). QA includes an annual TB risk assessment and review of pharmacist findings.

citations.title: Staffing Plan
citations.requirement: No numeric ratio. Written staffing plan covers scheduled and unscheduled needs 24 hours a day. Staff are present whenever a resident is in the building. Awake overnight staff are required when the Resident Assessment Tool triggers it. Dated schedules are kept on site for 18 months. On-site nursing is required only when ordered.

citations.title: Assisted Living Manager
citations.requirement: Manager is age 21+ with a high school diploma and is licensed. Level 3 has added education and experience requirements. Manager needs a current background check, TB screening, MMR/varicella immunity, first aid and CPR.

citations.title: 80-Hour Assisted Living Manager Training Course
citations.requirement: Manager completes the OHCQ-approved 80-hour course and exam. Manager also completes 20 hours of CE every 2 years.

citations.title: Alternate Assisted Living Manager
citations.requirement: Alternate is age 21+ with 2 years of health-related experience and the .19B(1)–(7) staff qualifications. Alternate takes over when the manager is unavailable.

citations.title: Other Staff - Qualifications
citations.requirement: Age, TB/MMR/varicella evidence, background check within 30 calendar days before employment, and initial and annual training. Also first aid and CPR, delegating-nurse competency for personal care, relief staff, proof of training, and 6-hour/2-hour cognitive impairment, mental illness and behavioral health training.

citations.title: Personnel Records
citations.requirement: Lists the required contents of each personnel file. Includes the criminal history records check, TB/immunity evidence, flu and COVID-19 vaccine advised, licensure, training, and an OIG exclusion list check before hire.

citations.title: Delegating Nurse
citations.requirement: Signed RN agreement and Board of Nursing delegating nurse course. RN is on site to observe each resident at least every 45 days. RN is on call at all times (or an alternate is). RN has clinical oversight, issues nursing orders and reviews the manager's assessments.

citations.title: Preadmission Requirements
citations.requirement: Resident Assessment Tool completed within 30 days before admission. Assessment is reviewed every 6 months.

citations.title: Admission Requirements
citations.requirement: No discrimination by race, color, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, physical disability or mental disability (§A). Do not admit anyone needing more than intermittent nursing care, stage 3 or 4 ulcer treatment, ventilator services, skilled monitoring with a fluctuating acute condition, or monitoring of an uncontrollable chronic condition (§B). Do not admit a person who is dangerous or at high risk that cannot be managed (§C). Hospice exception in §D.

citations.title: Resident-Specific Level of Care Waiver
citations.requirement: Section number and title confirmed in the chapter index. The text was not read for this deliverable. Confirm the procedure before finalizing the retention policy.

citations.title: Payment of Funds Before Admission
citations.requirement: Section number and title confirmed in the index. The text was not read. Confirm the deposit rules before finalizing the fee and refund policy.

citations.title: Resident Agreement - General Requirements and Nonfinancial Content
citations.requirement: Section number and title confirmed in the index. The text was not read. Use the OHCQ sample resident agreement template, which the checklist cites to .26–.27.

citations.title: Resident Agreement - Financial Content
citations.requirement: Resident agreement states financial terms. At least 45 calendar days' notice of a rate increase.

citations.title: Service Plan
citations.requirement: Service plan within 30 calendar days of admission. Based on the Resident Assessment Tool and nursing assessment. Full assessment within 48 hours after a significant change or nonroutine hospitalization, and at least annually. Review every 6 months. Special care needs are addressed (falls, pressure ulcers, diabetes, oxygen, enteral feeding, catheter, ostomy, mental illness, behaviors). Resident and representative are invited to meetings.

citations.title: Resident Record
citations.requirement: Contents of the resident record. Delegating nurse reassesses within 48 hours of readmission. Care notes at least weekly and on events. Record kept 5 years after discharge. Confidentiality and disposal follow HG Title 4, Subtitle 3.

citations.title: Services
citations.requirement: Three meals plus snacks daily. Menus written a week ahead, posted and kept 6 months. Dietitian or nutritionist reviews the 4-week menu before licensure and every 3 years. Personal care services are defined at §E.

citations.title: Medication Management and Administration
citations.requirement: Unlicensed staff who administer medications complete the Board of Nursing medication technician course and are certified. Self-administration assessment with quarterly delegating-nurse reassessment. Regimen review within 14 calendar days of admission. Pharmacist on-site review every 6 months for residents on 9+ medications. Delegating nurse on-site review every 45 calendar days. Storage and documentation rules. Controlled substances are counted each shift, double-locked and destroyed on site.

citations.title: Alzheimer's Special Care Unit
citations.requirement: Submit the Alzheimer's Special Care Unit Disclosure Form and get OHCQ's written approval before operating. Awake overnight staff are mandatory (§.14E(4)).

citations.title: Incident Reports
citations.requirement: Complete an incident report within 24 hours of knowledge. Reports are available on premises to OHCQ. Required content and notifications. Notify OHCQ within 24 hours of a resident death resulting from abuse, neglect, wandering, elopement, medication error, burns or any injury incurred at the program.

citations.title: Relocation and Discharge
citations.requirement: 5 calendar days' notice and consent for nonemergency relocation within the facility. 30 calendar days' notice before nonemergency discharge. Discharge planning and transfer documents. Emergency data sheet for acute transfer. Final statement, refunds and return of property within 30 calendar days. Attorney General may investigate funds abuse.

citations.title: Resident Representative
citations.requirement: Section number and title confirmed in the index. The text was not read. Confirm the list of recognized representatives before finalizing.

citations.title: Resident's Rights
citations.requirement: Resident Bill of Rights with rights (a)–(aa). Give it to residents and representatives before or upon admission and post it or post where it is located. Confidentiality. Work only with consent and compensation. Adult day care attendance is voluntary and its policies are disclosed in the resident agreement.

citations.title: Abuse, Neglect, and Financial Exploitation
citations.requirement: Written prohibition policies. Report within 24 hours to law enforcement, OHCQ, the Ombudsman or area agency on aging, local Department of Human Services/APS, and the manager. Up to a $1,000 penalty if not reported within 3 days. Investigate and document on site. Post reporting signs. Do not knowingly employ individuals with harmful criminal history.

citations.title: Restraints
citations.requirement: No restraint for discipline or convenience. Physician order stating purpose, type and duration. No PRN restraint orders. Reposition and toilet at least every 2 hours. Renew every 7 calendar days. Delegating nurse trains staff. Bed rails may be restraints. Notify family or representative each time. No improper chemical restraint. Hospice coordination in §H.

citations.title: Protection of a Resident's Personal Funds
citations.requirement: May manage funds only on the resident's or agent's express written request. Interest-bearing account for $300 or more. Bond, letter of credit or net assets equal to the average monthly balance (State as obligee).

citations.title: Misuse of Resident's Funds
citations.requirement: Section number and title confirmed in the index. The text was not read. Confirm before finalizing.

citations.title: Approval of Burial Arrangements for Unclaimed Deceased Residents
citations.requirement: Section number and title confirmed in the index. The text was not read. Confirm the approval procedure before finalizing the death policy.

citations.title: General Physical Plant Requirements
citations.requirement: Section number and title confirmed in the index. The text was not read. Confirm before finalizing the maintenance policy.

citations.title: Water Supply
citations.requirement: Resident hot water is 100–120°F at the fixture, with anti-scald or mixing valves.

citations.title: Security
citations.requirement: Section number and title confirmed in the index. The text was not read. Confirm before finalizing the elopement and security policy.

citations.title: Assist Rails
citations.requirement: Assist rails on both sides of resident corridors for programs of 17 or more beds (.46B per the research checklist).

citations.title: Emergency Preparedness
citations.requirement: NFPA 101 and local codes. Extinguishers on each floor and in special hazard areas, serviced annually by a State Fire Marshal licensee. Staff trained in extinguisher use initially and annually. Emergency Preparedness Packet. 72-hour continuity. Tracking system and medical fact sheet. Plan reviewed annually. Evacuation sites and transportation agreements. Staff oriented within 24 hours. Quarterly fire drills on all shifts and semiannual disaster drills on all shifts, records kept 2 years. Generator for 50+ residents.

citations.title: Smoking
citations.requirement: Written smoking policy stating whether smoking is permitted. If permitted: fire-safe rules, designated areas, no smoking where oxygen or flammables are used or stored, and resident smoking assessment and annual reassessment in the service plan.

citations.title: Common Areas, Resident Rooms, Bathrooms
citations.requirement: Common space of 35 sq ft per bed. Public restrooms and COMAR 10.15.03 food service at 17+ beds. Maximum 2 residents per room, 80/120 sq ft. 1 toilet and sink per 4 residents and 1 tub/shower per 8.

citations.title: Laundry
citations.requirement: Section number and title confirmed in the index. The text was not read. Confirm before finalizing the laundry procedures.

citations.title: Sanctions; Civil Money Penalties
citations.requirement: Sections confirmed in the index (.57 Sanctions, .58–.60 Civil Money Penalties). The text was not read. Cite only generally in compliance policy.

citations.title: Criminal Penalties
citations.requirement: Operating without a license is a criminal offense. OHCQ gives 30 days' written notice to comply where residents were not harmed.

citations.title: Waiver eligibility and cost of care
citations.requirement: Waiver resident may be charged room and board of up to $420/month. The waiver pays services only (§D).

citations.title: Requirements for assisted living waiver providers
citations.requirement: At least 1 staff per 8 residents in the daytime. Manager qualifications (physician, RN, LPN or 3 years of direct care). Alternate manager. Insurance if transporting residents. Cooperation with quarterly case-manager visits.

citations.title: Covered assisted living services
citations.requirement: Defines covered assisted living services under the waiver. Room and board are excluded.

citations.title: HCBOW payment procedures
citations.requirement: Payment is the lesser of the customary charge or the Medicaid rate.

citations.title: Delegation of nursing functions (Board of Nursing)
citations.requirement: Medications administered by unlicensed staff must comply with this chapter (cross-referenced in COMAR 10.07.14.31C and K). Text not independently read.

citations.title: Medication technician certification (Board of Nursing)
citations.requirement: Medication technician training and certification are documented in the personnel file (cross-referenced in COMAR 10.07.14.31B). Text not independently read.

citations.title: Maryland Confidentiality of Medical Records Act
citations.requirement: Resident medical records are released and disposed of as permitted by this subtitle (cross-referenced in COMAR 10.07.14.29H). Text not independently read.

citations.title: Criminal history records check
citations.requirement: Basis for the staff criminal history records check documented under COMAR 10.07.14.20I. Text not independently read.

citations.title: Immunity for good-faith reporters
citations.requirement: Civil immunity for a person who reports abuse, neglect or exploitation in good faith (cross-referenced in COMAR 10.07.14.37F). Text not independently read.

citations.title: Food service facilities
citations.requirement: Applies to programs with a licensed capacity of 17 or more beds. Smaller programs follow the basic food safety rules in COMAR 10.07.14.48 and any directive from OHCQ or local jurisdiction.

citations.title: General hospice care programs
citations.requirement: Hospice and the assisted living program each comply with their own chapter when a resident is under hospice care in the program (COMAR 10.07.14.38H). Text not independently read.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body, Assisted Living Manager and Alternate Manager Responsibilities
state_specifics: Licensee is the legal entity named on the OHCQ license. Keep the SDAT good-standing certificate current, because OHCQ may void the license 60 days after notice of non-compliance (.08H).
Licensed assisted living manager required from July 1, 2026 (Health Occ. §9-3A-01). Manager is age 21+ with a high school diploma (.15A).
Level 3 manager needs a 4-year degree, or 2 years in health care plus 1 year as manager, or 2 years in health care plus the 80-hour course (.15).
Alternate manager is age 21+ with 2 years of health-related experience and the .19B(1)–(7) qualifications (.18).
Manager signs a delegating-nurse agreement and meets the delegating nurse every 6 months (.13A(2)(b)).

policies.title: Licensure, Posting, Uniform Disclosure Statement and Regulatory Compliance
state_specifics: License names both a bed count and a level (1, 2 or 3). Never exceed either (.04, .05).
Post the license in a common-use area, with the manager's Board license verification (.04G).
Uniform Disclosure Statement is given free on request and amended within 30 days of any service change (.10).

Report building, fire or sanitary code citations to OHCQ within 7 days. Get OHCQ approval before adding beds or raising the level. Give 60 days' notice (49 or fewer beds) of ownership change, relocation or closure (.08).
OHCQ annual survey, extendable to 18 months with no open plan of correction, complaint, penalty or sanction (.12). Plan of correction due in 10 business days if cited (application Step Three).
Licensure standards waiver: written request, OHCQ decision within 45 days (.09).

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
state_specifics: Emergency and disaster plan must be reviewed at least annually (.47C(6)). Set the same annual review for the full manual.

OHCQ Step Three survey reviews 12 required written policies: bed and room assignment, change in accommodation, transfer, discharge, resident termination request, documentation, complaint and grievance, adult medical day care, abuse/neglect/financial exploitation, smoking, emergency and disaster plan, and quality assurance plan. Keep these current and indexed.
Version-control the manual and record the date each policy was last reviewed.

policies.title: Quality Assurance Plan and Performance Improvement
state_specifics: Written quality assurance plan is required (.13A).
Manager and delegating nurse meet and document every 6 months to review resident changes and pharmacy findings (.13A(2)(b)).
Pharmacist review documentation is reviewed every 6 months as part of QA (.31I(3)).
Include an annual TB risk assessment in the QA plan.
Trend incident reports (.33), falls, medication errors, grievances and drill results.

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
state_specifics: Check the federal HHS-OIG List of Excluded Individuals/Entities before hiring every employee and document it (.20O).
Allegations of financial exploitation are reported within 24 hours (.37C) and may be referred to the Medicaid Fraud Control Unit of the Attorney General (.37E(2)(b)).
Waiver payment is the lesser of the customary charge or the Medicaid rate (10.09.54.22).
Resident funds are kept separate from facility funds and protected by bond, letter of credit or net assets (.39).
Waiver claims are billed through LTSSMaryland from Oct. 1, 2026. Helpdesk 1-855-463-5877.

policies.title: Medicaid Community Options (HCBOW) Waiver Participation and HCBS Settings
state_specifics: Enrollment is through MPRIME (live Oct. 13, 2026), which requires an SDAT number in good standing. Helpdesk 1-844-463-7768. OLTSS 410-767-1739.
Waiver registry intake is through Maryland Access Point, 844-627-5465.
Rates effective July 1, 2024 (PT 04-25): $90.74/day Level II (W0226) and $114.51/day Level III (W0227). Confirm current rates before billing, as FY2026 LTSS rates were reported unchanged.
Room and board charged to a waiver resident may not exceed $420/month (10.09.54.03D). The waiver pays services only.
Provider standards: at least 1 staff per 8 residents in the daytime. Manager qualifications. Alternate manager. Insurance if transporting. Quarterly case-manager visits (10.09.54.05).
Confirm with OLTSS whether a Level 1-licensed program can enroll.

policies.title: Resident Bill of Rights and Responsibilities
state_specifics: Adopt a Resident Bill of Rights that includes at least rights (a)–(aa) of .36A(1).
Give it to every resident and representative before or upon admission. Post it conspicuously, or post a notice of where it is kept (.36A(2)).
Staff knock before entering a resident's room unless the resident is asleep or there is an emergency (.36A(1)(g)).

Rights include private visits (reasonable limits per the resident agreement and as posted by the manager), a private phone, unopened mail, choice of pharmacy, notice before a roommate change, and participation in transfer or discharge decisions.
Residents may not be assigned work without consent and appropriate compensation (.36C).

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: Residents may make complaints without threat or fear of retaliation and must get a prompt response through an established procedure (.36A(1)(q)–(r)).
Residents have access to the complaint procedures of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman, local Adult Protective Services, OHCQ and the protection and advocacy agency (.36A(1)(s)).
A written complaint and grievance policy is one of the 12 policies reviewed at the OHCQ survey.
Log each grievance, who handled it, the response date and the outcome.

policies.title: Ombudsman and Agency Access
state_specifics: Residents must have access to complaint procedures of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program (Dept. of Aging, COMAR 32.03.02), local APS, OHCQ and the designated protection and advocacy agency (.36A(1)(s)).
Post abuse and neglect reporting signs in employee and public areas (.37G).
Abuse reports go to the Ombudsman or local area agency on aging within 24 hours (.37C(1)(c)).

policies.title: Resident Agreement, Fees, Deposits and Refunds
state_specifics: Use the OHCQ sample resident agreement template with the required nonfinancial and financial terms (.26–.27). Disclose adult medical day care availability and policies in the agreement (.36D(2)).
At least 45 calendar days' notice of a rate increase (.27).
Within 30 calendar days of discharge give a final statement of account, any refunds due, and return all money and property (.34G).
Waiver residents may be charged up to $420/month room and board (10.09.54.03D).
Confirm the pre-admission deposit rules in .25 before finalizing.

policies.title: Resident Funds and Personal Property
state_specifics: The program may refuse to handle resident funds. If it handles funds, it needs the resident's or agent's express written request (.39B–C).
Deposit $300 or more in an interest-bearing account. Interest accrues to the resident. Keep resident accounts separate from facility accounts (.39).
Carry a bond, letter of credit or net assets equal to the average monthly balance. Keep the instrument or asset list on site for OHCQ (.39E).
Keep a transaction record for each resident (date, type, balance) and give residents statements on request.
On a change of ownership, the prior owner gives the new owner a certified audit and receipts (.39J).
Return funds and property within 30 calendar days of discharge (.34G).
Residents may keep personal clothing and effects with reasonable security (.36A(1)(n)).

policies.title: Advance Directives and MOLST
state_specifics: The resident record includes any advance directive, mental health advance directive and MOLST form (.29A(7)–(8)).
Attach advance directives, the MOLST form, powers of attorney and guardianship orders to the emergency data sheet that goes to an acute care facility (.34F(9)).
Residents may make an informed decision to accept or refuse treatment (.36A(1)(f)).
Do not give legal advice. Refer residents to counsel (.36A(1)(l)).

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Case discussion, examination and treatment are confidential and discreet. Only people directly involved in care may be present unless the resident or representative permits otherwise (.36B(1)).
Release records only with the consent of the resident or representative, or as permitted by HG Title 4, Subtitle 3. Exceptions are transfer to another facility and as required by law (.36B(2), .29H).
The manager shares resident information with the Department as needed (.36B(3)).
Determine whether the program is a HIPAA covered entity. Medicaid waiver electronic billing may make it one. If so, adopt the HIPAA privacy, security and breach procedures.
Dispose of records in accordance with HG Title 4, Subtitle 3 (.29H(3)).

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
state_specifics: Do not discriminate in admitting or providing care because of race, color, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, physical disability or mental disability (.23A).
Resident Bill of Rights provides for treatment with dignity and individuality (.36A(1)(a)).
Provide interpreter and translation access, and reasonable accommodation for residents with disabilities.
Admission screening may consider only the .23B–C criteria (care needs and safety), not protected characteristics.

policies.title: Resident Representative
state_specifics: Document the name and authority of any resident representative in the resident's record. Confirm the list of recognized representatives in .35 before finalizing.
Do not recognize a representative who exceeds the authority granted by the instrument or by State law.
Invite the representative to service plan meetings when the resident lacks capacity (.28A(5)).
Notify the representative of incidents (.33C(5)), restraint use (.38G) and relocation or discharge (.34).

policies.title: Adult Medical Day Care, Voluntary Programs and Resident Work Duties
state_specifics: Adult day care attendance or any structured program is voluntary (.36D(1)).
Adult medical day care availability and policies are disclosed in the resident agreement (.36D(2)). This is one of the 12 policies reviewed at survey.
Resident work duties need consent and appropriate compensation (or a documented decline of pay). Duties are described in the record, and the resident may stop at any time without retaliation (.36C).

policies.title: Pre-Admission Screening and Admission Criteria
state_specifics: Resident Assessment Tool is completed within 30 days before admission (.22).

Do not admit anyone who needs more than intermittent nursing care, treatment of stage 3 or 4 skin ulcers, ventilator services, skilled monitoring with a fluctuating acute condition, or monitoring of an uncontrollable chronic condition (.23B).
Do not admit anyone who is dangerous to self or others (when danger cannot be eliminated) or at high risk for health or safety complications that cannot be managed (.23C).
Hospice exception: .23B–C do not apply when a licensed general hospice program delivers the services through its plan of care (.23D).
Admission is within the licensed level of care (.05).
Medication regimen review within 14 calendar days of admission (.31F).

policies.title: Bed and Room Assignment and Change in Accommodation
state_specifics: Do not relocate a resident within the facility except under the resident agreement (.34A(1)).
Give at least 5 calendar days' notice and obtain consent for a nonemergency relocation. Document in the record (.34A(2)–(3)).
No more than 2 residents per room. At least 80 sq ft single and 120 sq ft double (.50).
Notify residents before a roommate change and take their input where possible (.36A(1)(w)).
Bed and room assignment and change in accommodation are among the 12 policies reviewed at survey.

policies.title: Resident Assessment Tool and Reassessment
state_specifics: Initial assessment: Resident Assessment Tool plus nursing assessment (.22, .28B(1)).
Full reassessment within 48 hours after a significant change of condition or nonroutine hospitalization (as nursing practice and the resident's condition require), and at least annually (.28B(2)).
The delegating nurse may decide a full assessment is not needed within 48 hours. Document the reasons and complete it within 7 calendar days (.28B(3)).
Review the assessment every 6 months. A score change in cognition/behavior, self-administration or communication requires practitioner evaluation and service plan changes (.28B(4)).
At each assessment, document whether awake overnight staff is needed (.28B(5)).
Readmission after hospitalization or a stay of 15+ days in a skilled facility, or after a significant change: delegating nurse reassesses within 48 hours (.29B).
Self-administering residents are reassessed quarterly by the delegating nurse (.31D(2)).

policies.title: Service Plan
state_specifics: Written service plan within 30 calendar days of admission. It states the services, when and how often, and how and by whom (.28D).
Review at least every 6 months, and sooner when condition or preferences change significantly (.28D(3)).
Invite the resident, and at the resident's request a representative or family member, to every plan meeting. Accommodate participants' schedules where possible (.28A).
Address special care needs: falls, pressure ulcer risk, diabetes, oxygen, enteral feeding, Foley catheter, ostomy, therapeutic medication levels, mental illness and disruptive behaviors (.28C).
Residents who smoke are assessed, and the plan documents any help or supervision needed (.48B(4)–(5)).

policies.title: Retention Limits and Conditions the Facility Cannot Serve
state_specifics: Retention is limited by the licensed level (.05) and the .23B–C conditions. A resident who develops these conditions needs reassessment and a plan to meet the need or discharge.
Hospice may supply services otherwise excluded by .23B–C (.23D).
Resident-specific level of care waiver: see .24. Confirm the procedure before finalizing.
If a special diet is beyond the program's capability, the resident or physician must make other arrangements or the program discharges (confirm current .30 text).
Discharge follows .34 (30 calendar days' notice, nonemergency).

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Relocation Notice
state_specifics: Notify the resident or representative within 30 calendar days before a nonemergency discharge. In an emergency, notify as quickly as possible and document the reason and the abbreviated notice (.34B).
Involuntary discharge or transfer must follow the resident agreement (.34B(1)). Residents have a right to notice, procedural fairness and humane treatment (.36A(1)(aa)).
Develop a safe discharge plan that considers the resident's needs and preferences (.34C).
Send the receiving facility, or give the resident for a home discharge: emergency data sheet, current medication and treatment orders, MARs and the most current Resident Assessment Tool (.34D–E).
Acute transfer: send the emergency data sheet with advance directives, MOLST, POA and guardianship papers (.34F).
Within 30 calendar days of discharge give the final account and refunds and return property (.34G). Attorney General may investigate funds abuse (.34H).

policies.title: Resident-Requested Termination and Move-Out
state_specifics: Resident termination request is one of the 12 policies reviewed at survey. Notice periods follow the resident agreement (.26–.27). Confirm the content before finalizing.
Within 30 calendar days of the move-out, give the final statement of account and refunds and return funds, property and valuables (.34G).
Provide the resident with continuity-of-care information when the resident moves home or to another setting (.34D–E).

policies.title: Medication Management, Storage and Disposal
state_specifics: Store medications in the original dispensed container, in a secure location, at the proper temperature (.31L).
Keep for each medication: resident name, medication, reason, dose, frequency, route, prescriber, issue date, expiration date, refill limits and directions (.31L(3)).
Only sealed, unopened packages or unit-dose blisters may be returned to the pharmacy (.31N).
Count Schedule II–V controlled substances before the close of every shift, with a witness. Keep them double-locked. Do not return them to the pharmacy (.31P).
Obtain a Controlled Dangerous Substances registration certificate from the Office of Controlled Substances Administration when required (.31P(4)).

Destroy controlled substances on site with two staff, one of whom is a licensed practitioner, pharmacist, RN, LPN, CMT or licensed manager. Record it on the Division of Drug Control form and send a copy within 10 calendar days (.31P(7)).
Pharmacist on-site review every 6 months for residents on 9+ medications, including OTC and PRN. Document it in the chart and review it in QA (.31I).
Manager develops written theft and diversion procedures covering storage, accountability, access, destruction and reporting (.31P(5)).

policies.title: Medication Administration, Medication Technicians and Self-Administration
state_specifics: Unlicensed staff who administer medications must first complete the Board of Nursing medication technician course taught by an approved RN, and be certified (.31A–B; COMAR 10.39.04). Manager documents this in the personnel file.
Certification renews every 2 years with 100 practice hours and a 4-hour update (MBON).
Administer only per current signed medical orders and professional standards (.31M). All administration complies with COMAR 10.27.11 (.31C).
Delegating RN on-site review at least every 45 calendar days (.31K).

Initial assessment determines whether the resident self-administers, self-administers with reminders or physical help, or needs staff administration (.31D). Self-administering residents are reassessed quarterly by the delegating nurse.
A resident may give medications to a spouse or domestic partner in the same program only with a practitioner assessment, quarterly delegating-nurse assessments and signed orders (.31E).
Record administration at the time the resident takes the medication (.31O).

policies.title: Nursing Services and Delegating Nurse
state_specifics: Signed agreement with an RN who completed the Board of Nursing delegating nurse course. Keep proof on file (.21).
RN observes each resident on site at least every 45 days and is on call at all times, or a qualified alternate is (.21C).
RN manages clinical oversight, issues nursing orders, reviews the manager's assessments and delegates tasks (.21C).
If the manager does not carry out nursing orders without identifying alternatives, the RN notifies the physician, OHCQ and the resident or representative. Confirm in current .21.
Manager and RN meet every 6 months (.13A(2)(b)).
On-site nursing beyond these duties is required only when ordered by the delegating nurse or a practitioner (.14).
Nursing services follow the Nurse Practice Act (Health Occ. Title 8). Personal care staff other than CNAs/GNAs show competence to the RN before working alone (.19C).

policies.title: Change of Condition, Practitioner Notification and Hospital Transfer
state_specifics: Information on a resident's condition, preferences or significant change is documented and communicated promptly to the resident, representative and the practitioners and staff involved (.29C).
Write care notes at least weekly, and on any significant change, transfer, return from appointments, practitioner visits, nonroutine leave and discharge (.29D).
Full reassessment within 48 hours after a significant change or nonroutine hospitalization (.28B(2)).

Emergency data sheet goes with the resident to an acute care facility and includes diagnoses, medications, allergies, diet restrictions, practitioner and representative contacts, and attached directives and MOLST (.34F).
Incident report within 24 hours when an incident occurs, with notification of the practitioner and the delegating nurse (.33).

policies.title: Alzheimer's Special Care Unit and Dementia / Memory Care
state_specifics: A memory care unit is an Alzheimer's Special Care Unit. Submit the Disclosure Form and obtain OHCQ's written approval before operating (.32).
Awake overnight staff are mandatory in an Alzheimer's unit. OHCQ may not waive this for an electronic monitoring system (.14E(4)).

Personal care staff receive 6 hours of cognitive impairment, mental illness and behavioral health training within 120 calendar days. Others receive 2 hours. Annual follow-up is 2 hours (personal care) or 1 hour (others) (.19H).
Training covers communication, behavioral intervention, de-escalation, meaningful activities, family interaction, end-of-life care and staff stress (.19H(2)).
Service plan addresses behaviors likely to disrupt or harm the resident or others (.28C(10)).
Do not use chemicals or drugs in excessive dose or duration, without indication, or with adverse consequences (.38C). Do not restrain for discipline or convenience (.38D).

policies.title: Falls Prevention
state_specifics: Service plan addresses fall risk or frequent falls with increased monitoring and intervention (.28C(1)).
Falls are incidents. Complete the report within 24 hours (.33A). Notify OHCQ within 24 hours if a resident dies from an injury incurred at the program (.33D(7)).
Manager monitors daily that the service plan is implemented and that ambulation devices and adaptive equipment work (confirm current .30 text).
Bed rails may be restraints. Document the determination for each resident (.38F).
Assist rails on both sides of resident corridors in programs of 17+ beds (.46B).

policies.title: Skin Integrity and Pressure Injury Prevention
state_specifics: Service plan addresses pressure ulcer risk, prevention and treatment (.28C(2)).
Do not admit a person who requires treatment of stage 3 or 4 skin ulcers, except under a hospice plan of care (.23B(2), .23D).
Keep monthly weights, or weights per practitioner order, in the record (.29A(9)).
Report skin changes to the delegating nurse. A significant change triggers a full reassessment within 48 hours (.28B(2)).

policies.title: Hospice and Home Health Coordination
state_specifics: When a resident is under a licensed general hospice program in the facility, the hospice and the assisted living program each comply with COMAR 10.07.14, COMAR 10.07.21 and federal rules (.38H).
Admission exclusions in .23B–C do not apply to hospice residents whose hospice plan of care delivers those services (.23D).
Manager facilitates access to home health, hospice, rehabilitation, skilled nursing and other services identified in the assessment. Confirm the current .30 subsection.
Record hospice orders, MOLST and care notes in the resident record (.29).

policies.title: Death of a Resident
state_specifics: Notify OHCQ within 24 hours of a resident death resulting from abuse, neglect, wandering, elopement, medication error, burns or any injury incurred at the program (.33D).
Complete an incident report within 24 hours (.33A). Report suspected abuse or neglect within 24 hours to all .37C parties.
Document the death, the location and the manner in a care note (.29D(1)(h)). Honor the MOLST and advance directives.
Within 30 calendar days give the final statement and refunds to the resident's agent and return property and valuables (.34G).
Burial of an unclaimed deceased resident requires approval under .41. Confirm the procedure before finalizing.
Keep the record 5 years (.29E).

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Financial Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Written policies prohibiting abuse, neglect and financial exploitation (.37A). This is one of the 12 policies reviewed at survey.
Do not knowingly employ anyone with a criminal conviction or history that indicates behavior potentially harmful to residents (.37B).
Report within 24 hours to law enforcement, OHCQ, the Ombudsman or area agency on aging, local DHS/APS and the manager (unless the manager is suspected) (.37C(1)).
Penalty up to $1,000 for failing to report within 3 days (.37C(2)). Licensed or certified individuals who fail to report may be referred to their board (.37C(4)).
Investigate thoroughly, keep written documentation on site and protect residents during the investigation (.37D).
Send investigation reports to law enforcement, OHCQ, the Ombudsman/AAA and APS. Referral may go to the State's attorney or the Medicaid Fraud Control Unit (.37E).
Good-faith reporters have immunity (HG §19-347(g)). Post reporting signs in employee and public areas (.37G).

policies.title: Incident and Accident Reporting
state_specifics: Staff complete an incident report within 24 hours of knowledge (.33A).

Each report includes time, date and place, individuals present, a complete description, staff response, and notification of the resident or representative, practitioner, delegating nurse and licensing or law enforcement authorities when appropriate. It also records follow-up and prevention steps (.33C).
Reports are kept on premises and available to OHCQ and designated agencies (.33B).
Notify OHCQ within 24 hours of a resident death caused by abuse, neglect, wandering, elopement, medication error, burns or injury incurred at the program (.33D).
Use the .02B definition of "incident".

policies.title: Elopement and Missing Resident
state_specifics: Notify OHCQ within 24 hours of a resident death from wandering or elopement (.33D).
Incident report within 24 hours for any elopement (.33A).
Awake overnight staff when the Resident Assessment Tool requires it. An electronic monitoring waiver is not available on an Alzheimer's unit (.14).
Use the emergency tracking system and resident identification in .47C(3)–(5).
Security requirements are in .45. Confirm the text before finalizing the door and alarm procedures.
Reassess wandering residents and update the service plan (.28C(10)).

policies.title: Restraints and Restrictive Practices
state_specifics: Residents have the right to be free from involuntary seclusion and from restraints used in violation of the chapter (.36A(1)(i), .38A).
No physical restraint for discipline or convenience, or without a physician's order treating a symptom or condition (.38D).
A restraint order states the purpose, type and duration. It must be time-specific, and PRN restraint orders are prohibited (.38E).
A restrained resident is repositioned and offered toileting at least every 2 hours. The order is renewed at least every 7 calendar days (.38E(4)–(5)).
Delegating nurse trains staff in the use of the ordered restraint (.38E(6)).
Notify the family or representative each time a restraint is used (.38G).
Bed rails may be restraints. Document the determination per resident (.38F). Protective devices as defined in .02B are not restraints (.38B).
Chemical restraint: no drugs in excessive dose or duration, without adequate indication, or despite adverse effects (.38C). Medication regimen review checks chemical restraint potential (.31G(2)).

policies.title: Emergency Preparedness and Disaster Plan
state_specifics: Develop an Assisted Living Emergency Preparedness Packet, readily available to all staff (.47C(1)).

Plan covers before, during and after: evacuation or shelter in place; notice to families and staff; staff coverage and assignments; and continuity of services including supplies for at least 72 hours (.47C(2)).
Resident tracking system: name, date and time sent, alternate location and a contact person with phone number (.47C(3)).

Brief medical fact sheet goes with each relocated resident: name, diagnosis, medications, allergies, diet, and family or legal representative contact. Review it monthly and keep it in a central location (.47C(4)–(5)).
Review the plan at least annually (.47C(6)). Documented agreements with evacuation sites and with transportation sources (.47C(7)–(8)).
Give the plan to local emergency management on request. Name an emergency planning liaison. Prepare an executive summary for residents and families on request (.47C(9)–(11)).
Staff are oriented to the plan within 24 hours of starting, with a signed record in the personnel file (.47E(1)).

Semiannual disaster drills on all shifts. Evacuation and shelter in place are each practiced at least once a year. A table-top exercise is allowed only if moving residents would be harmful. Records are kept 2 years (.47E(3)).
Programs with 50+ residents need an emergency generator with automatic transfer, tested monthly for 30 minutes and logged (.47F). Waiver requires disclosure to residents (.47F(7)).

policies.title: Fire Safety, Evacuation and Drills
state_specifics: Comply with local fire and building codes and NFPA 101, including Chapter 24 for one- or two-family dwellings (.47A).
Fire extinguishers on each floor and in or next to furnace rooms, boiler rooms, kitchens and laundries. Serviced annually by a State Fire Marshal licensee, with documentation on site (.47B).
Instruct staff in extinguisher use initially and at least annually (.47B(2), .19B(5)(a)).

Fire drills at least quarterly on all shifts. Records kept 2 years: date and time, participants and signatures, scenario, steps taken, successful and unsuccessful actions, and opportunities for improvement (.47E(2)).
Post individual floor plans with evacuation routes on each floor (.47D).
Fire inspection report is required for licensure. In Baltimore City and Baltimore County, programs of 1–16 beds submit the health department environmental report instead (application Step Two).
Staff trained in CPR are available 24 hours a day (.19D).

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Initial and annual staff training in infection control: standard precautions, contact precautions and hand hygiene (.19B(5)(b)).
Staff are free of communicable TB and immune to measles, mumps, rubella and varicella (.19B(1)). Annual TB risk assessment in the QA plan (.13).
Flu and COVID-19 vaccines are advised per CDC recommendations. Document surveillance of non-immune staff when local activity is elevated (.20K–L).
Food safety: fewer-than-17-bed programs follow the .48F(4) temperature rules (hazardous food at 45°F or below or 140°F or above; refrigeration 45°F or below; freezer 0°F or below).
Laundry procedures: see .55 (confirm text).
Adopt an OSHA bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan (29 CFR 1910.1030) for employees with occupational exposure.

policies.title: Smoking
state_specifics: Written smoking policy stating whether smoking is permitted (.48A). This is one of the 12 policies reviewed at survey.
If smoking is permitted: policies to minimize fire risk, and no smoking in hazardous locations or in any room where flammable liquids, combustible gases or oxygen are used or stored (.48B(2)(a)).
Designate smoking areas with ash trays of noncombustible, safe design. Areas comply with all local, State and federal regulations (.48B(2)–(3)).
Assess each resident who smokes for help or supervision needs and record it in the service plan. Reassess annually or after a change of condition (.48B(4)–(5)).
Smoking is in .48, not .47.

policies.title: Visitors, Visiting Hours and Pets
state_specifics: Residents may meet or visit privately with anyone they choose, subject to reasonable restrictions on hours and places stated in the resident agreement and posted by the manager (.36A(1)(p)).
Residents may retain and use personal effects, with reasonable limits for the health and safety of others (.36A(1)(n), (y)).

COMAR 10.07.14 has no pet-specific provision verified for this deliverable. Set operator rules for pets, covering vaccination, allergies and infection control, and apply .19B(5)(b) infection control training.
Visitors may need screening during outbreaks. Follow current CDC and MDH infection control guidance.

policies.title: Physical Plant Safety: Water Temperature, Security and Common Areas
state_specifics: Resident hot water is 100–120°F at the fixture. Use anti-scald valves (.43).
Resident rooms: maximum 2 residents, 80 sq ft single and 120 sq ft double of functional space (.50).
Bathrooms: 1 toilet and 1 sink per 4 residents and 1 tub or shower per 8 (.51).
Common space: 35 sq ft usable multipurpose space per licensed bed (.49). At 17+ beds, public restrooms and COMAR 10.15.03 food service compliance.
At 17+ beds, assist rails on both sides of resident corridors (.46).
Security (.45) and general physical plant (.42): confirm the text before finalizing the checklist.

policies.title: Food Service and Therapeutic Diets
state_specifics: Three meals plus snacks daily. Write menus a week ahead, post them and keep them 6 months (.30A).
A licensed dietitian or nutritionist reviews the 4-week regular menu before licensure and at least every 3 years (.30A(2)).
Prepare or arrange special diets as ordered. Record them in the resident record. Confirm current .30 text.
Programs of 17+ beds follow COMAR 10.15.03 and need a local food service permit. Smaller programs follow the .48F(4) food safety rules unless the jurisdiction or OHCQ directs otherwise.
Staff receive initial and annual basic food safety training (.19B(5)(c)).

policies.title: Activities and Social Programming
state_specifics: Services under .30 include social and leisure opportunities. Confirm the current .30 text for activity requirements.
Activities are tailored to resident preferences and capabilities in the service plan (.28A(2)).
Residents have the right to attend or decline religious services and to receive clergy visits (.36A(1)(m)).
Participation in structured programs and adult day care is voluntary (.36D(1)).
Cognitive impairment training includes making activities meaningful (.19H(2)(d)).

policies.title: Housekeeping, Laundry and Maintenance
state_specifics: Housekeeping and laundry requirements are in .30 and .55. Confirm the text before finalizing.
Physical plant must be maintained under .42. Anti-scald hot water 100–120°F (.43).
Extinguisher service annually (.47B). Generator testing monthly for 50+ residents (.47F).
Report code citations to OHCQ within 7 days (.08).
Kitchen requirements include space to wash, sanitize and store utensils and to store garbage cans (.49F).

policies.title: Transportation
state_specifics: Waiver providers who transport residents must carry insurance (10.09.54.05).
Manager provides or arranges transportation to activities per the service plan. Confirm the current .30 text.
Evacuation transportation sources require a documented agreement (.47C(8)).
Maintain driver qualifications and a vehicle inspection log.

policies.title: Staffing Levels, Staffing Plan and Supervision
state_specifics: No numeric ratio. Write a staffing plan based on residents' needs, covering scheduled and unscheduled needs 24 hours a day (.14).
A staff member is present whenever a resident is in the building or expected back (.14).
Awake overnight staff are required when the Resident Assessment Tool triggers it. Electronic monitoring may substitute with OHCQ approval, except on an Alzheimer's unit (.14).
Keep dated schedules on site for 18 months (.14).
Relief personnel are available at all times and meet .19B (.19E).
Waiver homes: at least 1 staff per 8 residents in the daytime (10.09.54.05).
Non-CNA personal-care staff may work up to 10 calendar days accompanied by a CNA, GNA or nurse-approved person while demonstrating competence (.19C).

policies.title: Background Checks and Exclusion Screening
state_specifics: Background check completed within 30 calendar days before employment, showing no criminal history indicating behavior potentially harmful to residents (.19B(2)).
Record the criminal history records check under HG §19-1901 in the personnel file (.20I).
Check the HHS-OIG List of Excluded Individuals/Entities before hire and document it (.20O).
Do not knowingly employ anyone with disqualifying history (.37B).
Verify licensure or certification (nurse, CNA, CMT, manager) with the issuing Board before hire (.19B(8), .20M).
Background checks also apply to owners, managers and household members at licensure (.07A(3)(d)).

policies.title: Hiring, Orientation and Ongoing Training
state_specifics: Orientation and ongoing training suited to resident needs (.19B(4)).
Initial and annual training in fire and life safety (including extinguishers), infection control, basic food safety and emergency disaster plans (.19B(5)).
First aid by a nationally certified instructor, with recertification every 2 years. Nurses are exempt (.19B(6)).
CPR with a hands-on component, for enough staff to have a trained person available 24 hours a day (.19D).
6 hours of cognitive impairment, mental illness and behavioral health training within 120 calendar days for personal-care staff, or 2 hours for others. Annual follow-up is 2 hours or 1 hour (.19H).
Staff are oriented to the emergency plan within 24 hours of starting, with a signed record (.47E(1)).
Proof of training includes the date, content, completion record, participation proof, and the trainer's signature, qualifications and contact (.19F).
Medication technicians: Board of Nursing 20-hour course, certified (.31A–B).

policies.title: Employee Health, TB Screening and Immunizations
state_specifics: Evidence that staff are free of communicable TB per the CDC health-care facility guidelines, and immune to measles, mumps, rubella and varicella by history or vaccination (.19B(1)).
Evidence that staff are free of impairment that would hinder their assigned duties (.19B(1)(c)).
Flu and COVID-19 vaccines advised per CDC recommendations. Document and keep surveillance of non-immune staff when local activity is elevated (.20K–L).
Manager needs a current TB screening and MMR/varicella immunity (.15).

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Each file has: name, age and gender; address and phone; education; employment history; reference notes; evaluations; attendance; emergency contact (.20A–H).
Criminal history records check (.20I). TB and immunity documentation (.20J). Flu and COVID-19 vaccine advised (.20K–L).
Licensure or certification (.20M). All required training and courses (.20N). OIG exclusion check before hire (.20O).
Medication technician training and certification (.31B). Emergency plan orientation signature (.47E(1)(b)).
Training proof elements (.19F).

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Staff must treat residents with consideration, respect and dignity (.36A(1)(a)).
Staff who witness or suspect abuse, neglect or exploitation must report within 24 hours. Licensed or certified staff who do not report may be referred to their board (.37C).
Staff knock before entering a resident's room (.36A(1)(g)). Respect confidentiality (.36B).
Residents may not be assigned work without consent and appropriate compensation (.36C).

Staff training includes resident's rights (.19B(7)(d)). The manager's obligations under .37 and .39 apply to financial dealings. A licensee who commits financial exploitation violates the chapter and applicable civil and criminal laws.
Gift, loan and financial-dealing rules are an operator policy, not set by a verified COMAR section.

policies.title: Assisted Living Manager Licensure, Training and Continuing Education
state_specifics: Manager licensure by the Board of Long-Term Care Administrators is required from July 1, 2026. Application fee $100 and license fee $200. State and FBI criminal history check required. Board: (410) 767-6500.
80-hour OHCQ-approved course with exam (HG §19-1807). 20 hours of CE every 2 years. Penalty up to $10,000.
Interim provisional period is up to 90 days, extendable up to 30 days (Health Occ. §9-3A-01(b)(2) per the enacted SB 613).
Keep the manager's Board license verification posted with the facility license (.04G).
Alternate manager: age 21+, 2 years of health-related experience, .19B(1)–(7) qualifications (.18).

policies.title: Resident Records and Retention
state_specifics: Keep a secure, confidential individual record for each resident at the program (.29A). It includes Resident Assessment Tools, nursing assessments, medical orders, service plans, care notes, emergency data sheet, advance directives, MOLST, monthly weights, pharmacy reviews and rehabilitation plans.

Care notes: on admission, at least weekly, on significant changes and incidents, on transfer, on return from appointments or nonroutine leaves, when seen by a practitioner, and at discharge. Notes are individualized, legible, dated, timed and signed (.29D).
Retain each record for 5 years after discharge (.29E). Arrange retention if the program closes (.29F).
On a change of ownership, the prior owner gives current-resident records to the new owner before the new license is issued (.29G).
Release and disposal follow HG Title 4, Subtitle 3 (.29H).
Related retention: staffing schedules 18 months (.14), drill records 2 years (.47E), menus 6 months (.30).

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Abuse, neglect or financial exploitation: within 24 hours to law enforcement, OHCQ, Ombudsman/AAA, local DHS/APS and the manager (.37C). Send investigation reports to the same agencies (.37E).
Resident death from abuse, neglect, wandering, elopement, medication error, burns or injury incurred at the program: notify OHCQ within 24 hours (.33D).

Changes to the license application: notify OHCQ immediately. Code citations: within 7 days. Ownership change, relocation or closure: 60 days' notice (49 or fewer beds). Bed or level increase: prior approval (.08).
Uniform Disclosure Statement amendment within 30 days of a service change (.10).
Delegating nurse termination: the prior version of the rule required notice to OHCQ. Confirm in current .21C before finalizing.
Controlled substance destruction form to the Division of Drug Control within 10 calendar days (.31P(7)).
Plan of correction within 10 business days of cited deficiencies (application Step Three).
Provide the emergency plan to local emergency management on request (.47C(9)).
